thread:
Morgan: Hey team — opened docs PR for the Responses API changes (link: https://git.redwood/infra/docs/pull/482). CI preview is stuck, reviewer request: @Sam or @Jia can you confirm default behavior for omitted "max_tokens" and streaming semantics? This is blocking merge.
Sam: On it. quick Q: current draft says "omitted max_tokens -> server chooses default (512)". Is that always true for streaming?
Morgan: That was the assumption I copied from the runtime PR notes, but I couldn't find an explicit statement. The preview link fails with a note about ambiguous example under streaming.
Jia: I can confirm server-side: when clients omit max_tokens we set a soft default of 512 for non-streaming responses. For streaming mode we intentionally treat omitted as "no explicit upper bound" (we still cap at model limit, e.g., 4096 for r-instruct-1). So behavior differs.
Alex: That difference needs a short callout in the API reference. Right now users will assume same default and might get infinite streams until a stop token.
Sam: Thanks @Jia — can you paste the small snippet of the runtime config we should cite? I'll add it to the PR.
Jia: Sure — paste this in the docs as an inline note: ```json
{"routing": {"response_defaults": {"max_tokens": 512, "streaming_omitted_means_unbounded": true}}}
``` Use that only as an illustration; actual config is internal.
Morgan: OK I'll add a clear bullet: "If max_tokens is omitted: non-streaming responses default to 512; streaming responses have no software-imposed default and are capped only by model maximum."
Sam: Also call out the edge-case when using function_call + streaming — the function call can close the stream early and we may return fewer tokens even if streaming is unbounded. Add an example.
Alex: Example suggestion for the docs (short): ```http
POST /v1/responses
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood-instruct-1",
  "stream": true,
  "input": "Generate a long list of examples",
  "function_call": "auto"
}
``` Then mention: "Because function_call may terminate generation once the function payload is complete, streaming output can stop before model token cap is reached."
Morgan: Added both notes and updated sample snippet. Pushed a small change to the PR to fix wording and to add an inline warning. 
DocsBot: Preview build started for PR #482 — staging URL: https://preview.redwood/docs/482 — status: building.
CI-Bot: Linkcheck failed: 2 broken links (one to internal runtime doc that is private). That is why preview is marked red.
Morgan: Hmm — that private link was in a footnote I added for reviewers. I'll move it to an internal-only doc and replace with a public note.
Sam: Once you replace the link, I can re-run the preview and give final approval. Also can we add a one-sentence migration note: "Previously clients relied on model defaults; new doc clarifies streaming versus non-streaming defaults" — for changelog.
Jia: Approving once wording is explicit about "model cap" vs "docs default". Small nit: use the phrase "model token limit" rather than "model maximum".
Alex: I'll do a quick grammar pass after the link is fixed. If preview passes, we can merge today; I'm available after 30m.
Morgan: Replaced the private link and updated the migration blurb. Pushed. @CI-Bot please re-run.
CI-Bot: Re-run triggered by Morgan. Linkcheck: OK. Preview URL updated: https://preview.redwood/docs/482 (green).
Sam: LGTM from me on the behavior text.
Jia: LGTM on accuracy.
Alex: Merged. :tada: Thanks everyone — that callout should cut down support tickets.
Morgan: Thanks all — closing the loop here.
